_doc: Controller tuning (src/control/). Units m, s, rad unless the key says otherwise. Every value here is a design choice, not a property of the corridor: the corridor itself is in corridor.json.
_Ts: s, control period: 20 Hz, the rate /joint_states arrives on the lab robot (check_robot.py, 23 Oct); the error model is discretised with it (Week 5 C5, models.error_model)
_v_nom: m/s, cruise speed: below the Waffle Pi's 0.26 m/s (ROBOTIS e-Manual); the LQR gain is designed at this speed (lqr.design_lqr). On the real robot commands are scaled down to robot_real.json v_max

lqr._doc: Bryson's rule (Week 6): Q_ii = 1/x_i_max^2, R = 1/u_max^2, x_max = the largest error we accept in normal driving, u_max = the largest correction we want to spend on it.
lqr._e_y_max: m, Bryson x_max for the cross-track error (Week 6 C.2); why 0.05 and not 0.10: lqr.design_weights docstring
lqr._e_theta_max_deg: deg, Bryson x_max for the heading error: a noticeable misalignment; larger and the camera starts to lose the markers (lqr.py)
lqr._d_omega_max: rad/s, Bryson u_max: the feedback correction we spend, well below the Waffle Pi's 1.82 rad/s (lqr.py)

lqi._doc: Integral action on e_y (Assessment 3 A.3). Off until the plain LQR shows a steady cross-track offset. z_max in m*s.

waypoints._doc: waypoints.py. arrive_tol: a waypoint counts as reached within this distance along the path [m]. turn_start_deg: corners sharper than this stop and turn on the spot. turn_done_deg: the turn ends when the heading error is below this. k_turn, w_turn_max: proportional turn-in-place gain [1/s] and its cap [rad/s]. slow_down_dist, v_min: start slowing this far before a stop [m], never below v_min while moving. a_max, alpha_max: rate limits on v [m/s^2] and omega [rad/s^2], placeholders until measured on the lab robot (same values as sim_env/drive_square_test.py).

docking._doc: docking.py. v_dock, v_min_dock [m/s]: approach speed and its floor; slow_down_dist [m]: start slowing this far from the stop range; stop_early [m]: stop this close to it (covers one step of travel). marker_max_age [s]: an ID 0 measurement older than this is not fresh (camera 15 Hz -> 3 frames). marker_lost_timeout, settle_timeout [s]: give up after this long. Complete when, for dock_hold_sec [s] in a row: |range - stop_range_base| <= dock_range_tol, |bearing| <= dock_bearing_tol (3 deg = about 1.9 cm sideways at the stop), lateral and heading error to goal_pose <= dock_lateral_tol [m] / dock_heading_tol_deg, the sd from P <= dock_pos_sigma_max [m] (sqrt(Pxx + Pyy)) / dock_heading_sigma_max_deg, and the encoder speeds are below the speed tolerances [m/s, rad/s].
docking._servo: ibvs: the LQR brings the robot onto the approach line, then image-based visual servoing (Week 9, src/control/visual_servo.py) takes the last part; pbvs: the LQR on the camera position all the way (the previous behaviour).
docking._camera_intrinsics: calibrated K and distortion used by IBVS (config/camera_real.json on the robot)
docking._ibvs_switch_range: m, base-to-marker range where IBVS takes over: W4 is 0.70 m out, so the LQR has 0.15 m to put the robot on the marker normal first (IBVS alone cannot remove a sideways offset, Week 9 D3/D4)
docking._ibvs_lambda: 1/s, IBVS gain: the feature error decays with a time constant of about 1/lambda = 1.25 s; lambda * camera period (67 ms) = 0.05 per frame keeps the loop far from the camera rate
docking._ibvs_w_max: rad/s, IBVS turn-rate saturation (Week 9 B3: saturate the twist, keep its direction), well below 1.82 rad/s
docking._ibvs_e_tol_px: px rms over the 8 corner coordinates: 1.5 px is about 4 mm of range at the stop (the marker is 189 px wide there)
docking._ibvs_still: IBVS also ends when |v| and |omega| stay below these for ibvs_still_sec: the residual the base cannot remove; the SETTLE checks then decide
docking._bumper_dist: m: in DOCK the forward command is held at 0 while the LiDAR sees anything closer than this in front of the robot's body (free_ahead), so the robot never pushes into the dock stand or a panel
docking._dock_bearing_tol_deg: deg, see the docking _doc: 3 deg is about 1.9 cm sideways at the 0.356 m stop of the design
docking._dock_linear_speed_tol: m/s: encoder speed below which the robot counts as stopped, about 5 encoder ticks per 50 ms step (4096 ticks/rev, r = 33 mm)
docking._dock_angular_speed_tol: rad/s: turn rate below which the robot counts as stopped (same tick resolution, over the 0.288 m track)

lidar_obs._doc: lidar_obs.py (stand-in for Perception's obs). Sectors in degrees in {B}, as the team plan; margin [m] each side of the robot for free_ahead; min_coverage = fraction of forward beams (+-90 deg) that must return for the scan to count as valid.
lidar_obs._left_sector_deg: deg in {B}: forward-left sector of the team plan's 'LiDAR output specification' (left_clear)
lidar_obs._right_sector_deg: deg in {B}: forward-right sector (right_clear), mirror of left_sector_deg

avoidance._doc: avoidance.py. trigger_dist [m]: start avoiding when free_ahead is below this; end_ignore [m]: ignore returns this close to the segment's end waypoint (the wall at the end of a leg). side_margin [m]: added to the robot half width (0.153 m) for its swept lane; clearance [m]: extra gap kept from the box. look_ahead [m]: how far ahead points count as the obstacle; box_depth [m]: assumed depth of an obstacle we cannot see behind; max_offset [m]: largest sideways shift allowed. ramp_len [m]: travel over which the offset ramps in and out; rejoin_ahead [m]: the original lane must be free this far ahead before rejoining. stop_dist [m]: stop if something is this close in front; max_scan_age [s]: do not move on an older scan (LiDAR 5 Hz). v_avoid [m/s]: speed while avoiding.
